Jobber's website is one of our most important growth engines — the place where small home-service businesses first meet the product and decide to start a trial. You'll work across our modern Jamstack stack (Next.js, Sanity headless CMS, React, TypeScript) as well as our traditional headful WordPress platform (PHP, Twig templates), expanding our component libraries and engineering high-performance CRO frameworks. CMS familiarity is essential: you'll build and optimize features across both modern headless APIs and legacy PHP/Twig codebases. This is a senior individual-contributor role with real technical influence: you'll set experimentation standards, mentor developers, and partner with the Engineering Manager on quality and site performance.

Just as importantly, we want someone who treats AI-assisted development as a core engineering skill. We're actively reshaping how we build — using AI coding agents, MCP-connected tooling, and automated workflows to move faster without sacrificing quality — and we want this person to help lead that evolution, not just keep up with it.

Build on a modern front-end stack

 - Own performance and accessibility as first-class requirements — Core Web Vitals, semantic and accessible markup, and fast, resilient page loads that directly support conversion.

 - Work seamlessly between headless and traditional CMS architectures — integrate APIs and structured content in Sanity while maintaining Twig-templated components in WordPress as we transition our web ecosystem.

 - Write well-tested, scalable, well-organized code and drive consistent engineering practices through code review.

 - Collaborate with our other developers on best technical practices and project decisions.

Push our AI-assisted workflow forward

 - Use AI coding tools and agents fluently (e.g. Claude, AI-assisted IDEs, agentic workflows) to accelerate development while keeping a critical eye on output quality and reliability.

 - Help define and benchmark team standards for AI-assisted development — identifying what works, documenting it, and raising the whole team's baseline.

Power experimentation and growth

 - Architect and execute complex A/B and multivariate experiments across high-converting marketing flows, partnering with CRO leads and data analysts to design statistically sound, performant test variants.

 - Build for experimentation velocity and statistical integrity — minimize flicker, ensure client/server-side rendering accuracy, and reduce time-to-market from test hypothesis to live variant.

 - Support experimentation with the technical foundations (structured data, performance, rendering) that use best practices

Raise the technical bar

 - Set patterns and technical direction for how we build, and bring the team along through pragmatic, well-reasoned decisions.

 - Mentor and coach other front-end developers, lifting their skills and holding the team to its engineering principles.

 - Partner with the Engineering Manager on technical standards, code quality, and architecture

 - Identify and act on opportunities to improve the stack, tooling, and processes, and maintain strong team documentation.

 - Deep front-end expertise. Expert command of HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, accessibility, and web performance, plus several years building production applications.

 - Proven web experimentation & CRO expertise. Hands-on experience architecting and shipping complex A/B, Multivariate Testing, and personalized web experiments with measurable conversion outcomes.

 - Experience with web experimentation and feature flag platforms (e.g. Kameleoon, Optimizely, VWO, LaunchDarkly) and product analytics tools (e.g. Amplitude, GA4).

 - Strong Jamstack and modern front-end stack. Mastery of Next.js, React, TypeScript, and modern rendering strategies with a focus on performance and accessibility.

 - Experience working within a design system or maintaining a shared component library.

 - Versatile CMS background (Headless Sanity & WordPress/Twig). Experience modeling content in headless CMS platforms (Sanity/Contentful) alongside hands-on proficiency in traditional WordPress, PHP, and Twig templates.

 - Hands-on AI-assisted development. You actively use AI coding tools in your day-to-day work and have a point of view on where they help, where they don't, and how to use them responsibly.

 - A growth and experimentation mindset. You're comfortable building for measurement and iteration, and you care about the business outcome your code drives.

 - Technical leadership without ego. You set standards and mentor others while staying collaborative and open to better ideas.

 - Strong communication. You collaborate easily with both technical and non-technical partners — designers, marketers, and CRO.

 - Ambitious and humble. You don't accept the status quo simply because "it's what we've always done" — you push for better, newer, more innovative approaches while staying grounded.

Nice to have:

Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com/ is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies — niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently — accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE:

You'll join Beacon's Portfolio Product team — a cross-functional group of Product Managers, Engineers, Designers, GTM experts, and Data Scientists working directly with our 40+ portfolio companies and counting (at roughly one new acquisition per week) to drive measurable outcomes through AI and software.

 

At the core, every PM at Beacon owns product outcomes for 2 to 5 portfolio companies at a time, acting as a hands-on, founding product leader embedded in each business. You'll sit close to the GM, the operators, and the customers, figure out where the leverage is, and ship software directly into the business. The best PMs don't just deliver for the companies they're deployed at — they compress what they learn into reusable playbooks that spread to every other portfolio company in the same vertical. The ultimate objective is to transform our portfolio companies into unicorns!

 

For the right candidates, this role grows beyond individual ownership. As your vertical scales, you may build and lead a team of PMs, take on hiring and coaching responsibilities, and become the person who sets product vision and standards across an entire industry segment — partnering directly with GMs, founders & operators, and driving planning across the whole portfolio. How much of that path applies to you depends on your background and trajectory, and we'll shape the role around what you bring.

 

This is not a consulting role. We ship software, not slides. The deliverable is a running system.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own product outcomes for 2 to 5 portfolio companies simultaneously, acting as a fractional/founding product leader embedded in each business

 - Lead quarterly and annual planning, helping teams set product visions and translate them into achievable goals

 - Build and maintain roadmaps that balance customer needs, business goals, and technical constraints

 - Drive sprint planning and execution, improving team velocity and predictability over time

 - Develop prioritization frameworks that help CEOs and operators make better product decisions

 - Build customer feedback systems that turn qualitative inputs into actionable roadmap decisions

 - Coordinate feature launches across engineering, sales, marketing, and support

 - Coach developers, designers, and early PMs to think like product managers

 - Distill learnings into cross-portfolio playbooks that scale impact beyond your assigned companies

 - Partner with GMs, founders, and operators to set product vision and translate it into executable roadmaps

 - Contribute to Beacon's broader AI platform by surfacing patterns and opportunities from your companies

 


AS YOUR SCOPE GROWS YOU MAY ALSO:

 - Build and lead a team of PMs, hiring, onboarding, and developing them as your portfolio scales

 - Codify cross-portfolio playbooks that turn individual wins into repeatable systems across an entire vertical

 - Set the bar for how great product work looks at Beacon — spec quality, customer discovery, prioritization rigor

 - Own product strategy and outcomes across a defined vertical, not just individual companies

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - BA/BS degree; MBA a plus

 - 4+ years of product management experience, ideally in B2B SaaS (senior candidates typically bring 7+ years, including 2+ years in a formal leadership role or as a co-founder)

 - Strong fundamentals: roadmapping, sprint planning, spec writing, prioritization frameworks

 - Sharp customer discovery instincts and the ability to identify high-impact opportunities fast

 - Comfortable managing multiple companies and stakeholders simultaneously

 - Ability to influence founders and executives without direct authority

 - For more senior candidates: a proven track record leading and developing other PMs, not just doing great PM work individually

 - Strong systems thinking — you see patterns across companies and know how to turn them into playbooks

 - High autonomy, low ego. You figure things out and get them done

 - Entrepreneurial mindset and genuine comfort with ambiguity


THIS ROLE IS PERFECT FOR YOU IF:

 - You are an ex-founder, or have founding PM / early product hire experience at a high-growth startup

 - You want real ownership over how businesses (and, over time, entire industry verticals) get transformed through software and AI

 - You get satisfaction from shipping great product yourself — and, as you grow, from building capability in others

 - You are commercially-minded and curious about private equity, rollups, and how profitable businesses are built


Our Values at Beacon Software

 - Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.

 - Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

AI does not make hiring decisions: Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Executive Operations (Exec Ops) Chief of Staff Track, 12–18 Months) 
 If you’re a highly organized, extremely self-accountable, love project management (think Trello/Asana), and desire to grow into the 2nd in command of a fast growing startup… then this might just be your dream job. 
 My name is Richard Yu, I’m the founder/CEO of a fast-growing education + software business. 
 Across all social, my media team and I have built a 1.5M+ follower platform (@richardyuzee on IG, as an example).
 My #1 responsibility is to spend 40 hours/week being the talent (face of our content), and visionary (having long blocks of 4 hrs/day) where I can think about vision and growth strategies.
 That means I need to spend all my time creating content, driving strategy, and making high-leverage decisions… and this is where you come in.
 Your job is to protect my time, eliminate operational drag, and make sure the company actually executes.
 This role is Exec Ops / Office of the CEO — think of it as a supercharged Executive Assistant with a real path to Chief of Staff, based on performance. You will be my execution arm and second brain, with high trust, high access, and high expectations.
 This is not a “cute admin” job. It’s also not a glamorous strategy-only job. It’s the real work: calendar, follow-ups, accountability, systems, project management, hiring ops, and getting things done
 What you’ll own (your responsibilities)
 1) CEO Time + Calendar (your #1 responsibility)
 Own my calendar ruthlessly: protect deep work blocks, batch meetings, enforce priorities
 Gate time, not people (you’re not allowed to be a “gatekeeper” personality)
 Turn chaos into an intentional weekly schedule that matches company goals
 2) Internal Communication + Follow-Up
 Run the follow-up engine: action items, owners, due dates, reminders, escalation
 Ensure nothing dies in Slack/WhatsApp/email because people “got busy”
 Draft messages/emails and internal updates so I can approve quickly
 3) Project Management + Accountability (across the whole org)
 Build/quarterback the company operating system (Trello/Asana/Notion—whatever we standardize)
 Every project has: owner, deadline, next action, definition of done
 Hold leaders accountable (ex: Moe accountable to deliverables, Bashar accountable to reporting cadence, content team accountable to output)
 4) Hiring Operations (big focus right now)
 Run end-to-end hiring ops for key roles: Organic Content Director, Senior DR Copywriter/Head of Marketing, IG Copywriter, etc.
 Manage pipeline, scheduling, scorecards, assignments, Loom reviews, references
 Keep the process moving fast without me getting dragged into logistics
 5) Content Operations Oversight (not creating content)
 Ensure content machines ship on time: YouTube, IG, email—whatever is on the calendar gets done on time. 
 Track weekly output + deadlines + approvals so I’m not chasing people 
 You must be insanely detail oriented and VERY good at calling people out and holding them accountable. 
 6) Metrics + Reporting
 Monthly P&L request/collection, KPI dashboards, and weekly reporting rhythm
 You will analyze the Profit & Loss statement every month, analyze the payroll (yes you will know how much everyone gets paid), and provide extremely detailed recommendations on who should get raises, comp structure adjustments, who is being inefficient, who needs to get cut, etc. 
 7) Personal + Local Projects (as needed)
 Help execute real-life projects that support business performance (ex: managing the build-out of a home studio in Puerto Rico)
 Spanish is preferred because it helps with local execution, but it’s not required. If you’re insanely quick with a translator / ChatGPT for messages, works as well. 
 8) AI Emphasis 
 You should come with batteries included with understanding how to use AI in your workflow. The most BASIC version of this is ChatGPT instead of using Google, that’s the bare bare minimum. 
 You should be so good with AI that you are now giving feedback and suggestions to OTHER department leaders on how they should be using AI in their day to day responsiblities. 
 What success looks like (KPIs)
 20+ hours/week of my time returned within 60–90 days
 I stop doing: project management, follow-ups, DM appointment setting, internal chasing, hiring logistics
 Weekly operating rhythm runs without me pushing it
 Projects move faster, less stress, fewer dropped balls
 The company becomes calmer and more accountable — not more chaotic
 Who this is for
 This is for you if:
 You’re an operator: you love execution, structure, and turning chaos into order
 You have extreme ownership: you don’t wait to be told, you anticipate
 You can make good decisions without asking me every day for permission.
 You’re comfortable being in the background while I’m front-facing in the content
 You’re discreet and trustworthy (you will see everything)
 You’re strong at writing and communication (VERY detailed reports, clear, direct)
 You enjoy running a tight system and holding people accountable
 Who this is NOT for
 This is not for you if:
 You want a “strategy-only” role where you get to “bounce ideas” with Richard without doing admin, follow-ups, or nitty-gritty execution
 You need constant direction, reassurance, or step-by-step instructions where you get “coaching” from Richard (FYI - you’re here to protect my time, not get “free mentorship” from Richard).
 You avoid conflict and can’t hold people accountable in tough conversations when they’re late or underperforming 
 You’re not comfortable with high access + high confidentiality
 You get offended by doing “unsexy” tasks — this role includes them. 
 Example: 3-4 hour project of looking at every single expense item on Richard’s AMEX credit card statement to identify for software and expenses that we are overpaying on, and then reaching out to each software company to cancel them. 
 You should be smart to DO IT ONCE, and either build a system to automate this, delegate to someone else, or you just own this ongoing monthly moving forward.

 coordinating hiring logistics and keeping candidates moving along by messaging them on iMessage and Whatsapp on my behalf
 Collecting metrics, reports, and making sure people deliver

 Expérience avérée dans un environnement formel de développement de projets;
 Expérience dans le domaine du transport en commun ou du transport sur rail, un atout.

Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.


Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 Organization Overview 
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a registered, charitable organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community based primary care, wellness services, and health education to Durham community members who face multiple barriers to their health and well-being. 
 DCHC also provides equity-based programs and services that focus on priority populations such as Indigenous, Black, the 2SLGBTQI Community, Newcomers to Canada, Seniors, and Unattached patients (i.e., those without a family doctor), to name a few. DCHC ensures Durham community members receive not only sick care, but preventive care as well.
 At DCHC, we are a team-based interprofessional group of staff including physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counselors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and other administrative staff. We always place every client at the centre of our approach to care, based on their needs. We address these needs through integrated clinical and wellness care and health education.
 It's an exciting time to be joining this organization.  Durham Community Health Centre has been selected as the lead agency for the new Homeless Addiction Recovery Treatment (HART) Hub in the Durham region.  This innovative hub will provide life-changing services for individuals struggling with addiction and mental health challenges, helping them regain stability and rebuild their futures. The Hart Hub is a 24/7 operation, providing continuous support to the community.
 Position Overview 
 As a member of an interdisciplinary team, the Nurse Practitioner (NP) will deliver comprehensive, client-centered primary care and addiction-focused health services to individuals experiencing homelessness and/or substance use challenges in the community.
 The NP will provide primary care assessments, diagnosis, and treatment of clients with complex physical, mental health, and substance use concerns – working collaboratively with internal and external providers to ensure integrated, wraparound supports aimed at improving access, reducing barriers, and addressing social determinants of health. The NP will activate clinical pathways, referring clients to additional DCHC services and connecting them with community- based and specialty services as indicated.

 Provide client-centered primary care in a non-judgmental manner, including clients as partners in their care, recognizing the social determinants of health and associated health risks, and taking the stance of a health advocate. 
 Actively participate, seek, and provide consultation within an inter-professional model of care 
 Perform clinical assessments and health information gathering for clients with complex needs 
 Provide nursing services that address the biopsychosocial needs of clients, including clients with multiple comorbid health conditions, mental health diagnoses and/or concurrent disorders involving substance use/abuse. 
 Perform intake assessment activities for new clients

 An overview of this role
 You'll be the Staff Program Manager, CCO Programs, running the cross-functional initiatives on the Chief Customer Officer's (CCO) priority list. These programs include go-to-market transformation, retention and renewal motions tied to major annual recurring revenue (ARR) goals, the field-to-product feedback loop, and executive engagement with our highest-value accounts. You'll turn executive intent into workstreams, coordinate senior stakeholders across Sales, Customer Experience, Product, Marketing, Renewals, Professional Services, Data, and Enablement, and make the tactical calls that keep the portfolio honest.
 This is a founding seat reporting to the CCO while the broader Programs function is built, and the reporting line may evolve as the team scales. In your first year, every CCO-level program will have a clear owner other than the CCO, leadership will trust your data-grounded view of program health, and the portfolio will deliver measurable business outcomes.
 What you'll do
 Own execution and business outcomes across CCO-level programs, including go-to-market transformation, renewal and retention motions, product feedback loops, and executive sponsorship for top accounts.
 Turn CCO direction into workstreams with clear owners, dependencies, and timelines.
 Coordinate senior stakeholders across Sales, Customer Experience, Product, Marketing, Renewals, Professional Services, Data, and Enablement, holding them accountable without direct authority.
 Surface stalled work, unowned risks, and slipping timelines so the CCO has a reliable, real-time view of the portfolio.
 Recommend scope changes, re-sequencing, or ending a program when it is not delivering value.
 Drive follow-through from executive meetings by tracking decisions and action items to completion.
 Track program health using data, connect execution to retention, expansion, adoption, and ARR outcomes, and communicate executive-ready narratives.
 Build shared standards for tracking, reporting, and handoffs, and iterate plans with functional leaders based on field feedback.
 What you'll bring
 Experience leading complex, cross-functional strategic programs at the executive level and turning ambiguous direction into delivered outcomes without a fully scoped brief.
 Experience in Customer Experience, go-to-market, or revenue-facing functions such as Customer Success, Renewals, Sales, or Revenue Operations, with fluency in retention, expansion, and adoption motions and how they contribute to ARR.
 The ability to influence senior stakeholders, including executives, and hold them accountable to commitments without formal authority.
 Judgment to make high-stakes tactical recommendations under ambiguity, including when data supports changing direction or ending a program.
 Data fluency to assess program health, diagnose where work is breaking down, and recommend a data-informed next step.
 Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to move between an executive-ready narrative and execution-level detail.
 Comfort operating without established infrastructure and helping build the function's operating model.
 Reliable follow-through and the ability to navigate conflict and competing priorities across a broad stakeholder group.
 About the team
 You'll be the first Program Manager supporting CX Executive initiatives and the founding hire in a Programs function that will grow as the CCO's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives outgrow ad hoc ownership. The team works across the customer lifecycle, from go-to-market strategy and product feedback through renewal, expansion, and executive relationships with large accounts. We partner with Sales, Customer Experience, Product, Marketing, Data, and Enablement leaders in a globally distributed, largely asynchronous environment to turn CCO commitments into shipped outcomes.
